about: Minimized regression vectors of the issue #196 differential fuzz: each divergence the campaigns found, minimized, and agreement vectors at boundaries the generated corpus does not cross (`agrees`: why both sides answer alike). `origin` says where a vector came from: the campaign case it was minimized from, or that it was written by hand (after a run-3 case of the first campaign, generator e62f427, whose inputs no commit on this branch regenerates). Each runs in its own environment (its `did`); the Rust driver records the reference verdict into tests/goldens/differential/corpus.jsonl, and the TypeScript replay holds each either to agreement (`agrees`) or to the exact symptom listed for its case id, with its issue, in tests/goldens/differential/divergences.json. A vector stays for good (#62): when its divergence is fixed, it becomes an agreement vector. A vector whose source candid-core's compiler refuses (an `opt`-only cycle, refused since #234; the reference still accepts the source) carries `contract`, the graph the compiler wrote for that source before #234 (`types`, `declarations`, an optional `actor`); the Rust driver builds that Contract through the model, as the Contract loaders still accept it, and marks the environment `compile_refused` with the compiler's code and the issue that decided the refusal. Such a vector names that issue in its own `compile_refused` (234 for an `opt`-only cycle), and the driver refuses a `contract` without it.
